01 / Thanh’s Journey

Thanh’s
journey.

Born in 2009, I grew up with LEGO bricks, people who encouraged my curiosity, and the joy of making something work.

01Early curiosity

From LEGO bricks to prototypes.

My love for STEM began with childhood LEGO bricks and a supportive mom who always created opportunities for me to explore my curiosity. When she enrolled me in my first technology and coding classes, I instantly felt at home. Loving communication and teamwork, I quickly bonded with new friends, and almost immediately, we were building our very first tech prototypes together. The thrill of bringing those early creations to life sparked an endless drive in me to keep inventing and crafting new things.

02Discovering physics

Understanding how things work.

Alongside building, science has captivated me since elementary school. To me, science, especially physics is more than just numbers and equations it is a deep, convincing logic that explains every detail of the world around us. As I grew older, my goal shifted from simply understanding how the world works to making it better. Today, I study Physics to lift theories off the page and turn them into tangible machines that support struggling families in remote highlands and help young students on their journey to school.

03People & purpose

Why I want to build.

My journey began with a sense of responsibility toward my own community, and every product I build stems from the smallest stirrings of empathy. At heart, I simply want to help people to bring electricity to families in remote highlands, and to give young children libraries filled with enough books to study and explore every day, just as I had growing up. Above all, I dream of a world where people are deeply connected, where everyone lives in warmth and happiness, and has the freedom to pursue what they truly love.

04Owner / Developer

PaveGuard

Because Vietnam has a tropical monsoon climate near the equator, summers become extremely hot and uncomfortable. Especially when people need to go outside, the scorching heat and extreme street temperatures are hard to gauge from inside air-conditioned, insulated homes. Even with weather forecasts, those systems only provide average temperatures across broad regions with a wide margin of error, making them unsuitable for checking specific local spots. Therefore, we developed a device that measures road surface temperature and humidity, helping residents accurately check real-time street conditions so they can plan ahead and take proper safety precautions before heading out.

05Co-owner / STEMese

FloodGuard

This time of year is when Vietnam experiences the highest frequency of severe storms and flash floods. Watching the news, I felt deeply saddened and empathetic toward the immense losses suffered by local communities losing their property, morale, and even loved ones. Rather than simply donating money or clothing like many others, our team wanted to create a product that addresses the root of the problem. Our breakthrough lies in targeting the core indicator of floods and storms: water levels. We engineered a device that rapidly alerts residents in surrounding areas whenever the water level rises by even a small increment, allowing them to respond and evacuate in time regardless of how far away they are. Furthermore, our device runs 100% on solar power eliminating the need for manual recharging and is fully resistant to rainwater, humidity, and environmental interference.

06Developer / Energy storage

Sand Battery

Noticing how much excess energy especially heat and sunlight escapes wasted into the environment while many families in the remote highlands still lack those exact sources of warmth and power, my team and I came together to build this Sand Battery.

At its core, the device features a chamber filled with sand. When it captures external thermal or solar energy, the heat warms up aluminum pipes inside the container, which in turn heats the surrounding sand. Because sand naturally retains heat remarkably well and is further reinforced by an outer shell we insulated with cotton wool and foam the system stores thermal energy with high efficiency. This stored heat can then serve the everyday needs of underprivileged households, from warming water for bathing to heating living spaces and assisting with cooking.

07What I learned at home

A family connection to service.

My grandfather’s story is a lasting inspiration. Returning from the war, he served as the director of an agricultural cooperative in Thanh Oai District, Hanoi City (previously Ha Tay Province), leading technical innovations in farming tools and machinery to drive local agricultural mechanization. Hearing him share how technical improvements boosted productivity planted the seeds for my own fascination with engineering. Those early conversations ultimately fueled my passion for Electrical Engineering and STEM, showing me the real-world impact of technological solutions.

A Legacy of Love, A Lifelong Mission

Looking back at my parents’ journey, I see more than a story of love. I see two people brought together by a shared belief that every community deserves the opportunity to thrive. Through their work with local NGOs in Vietnam’s mountainous border regions, they have helped mobilize clean water projects, supported women through economic empowerment and livestock training, and contributed to improving livelihoods in underserved communities.

Their love story began along this journey of service. United by a common purpose, they found in each other not only a life partner, but also a companion who shared their dreams and commitment to making a difference.

Growing up, I came to understand that community development is not a single project or a temporary act of kindness. It is a lifelong mission that requires patience, dedication, and the willingness to walk alongside others as they build a better future.

Today, I see their journey as a legacy entrusted to me one that I hope to carry forward in my own way. Their example has shaped my understanding of purpose, reminding me that the most meaningful impact is not simply what we give to a community, but what we help it build for generations to come.
